paragraphs.en: Dorothy lay down to rest after a long walk while the Woodman built a ladder from forest wood. The Lion curled up for sleep, and Toto lay beside him.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西在长途跋涉后躺下来休息，而木匠用森林里的木材搭起了一个梯子。狮子蜷缩着准备睡觉，托托则躺在他的旁边。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow watched as the Woodman worked, asking why the wall was there. "Rest your brains," replied the Woodman, "we'll know what's on the other side once we climb over it."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人看着樵夫工作，便问那堵墙的原因。“歇会儿吧，”樵夫回答说，“等我们翻过墙去就知道那边有什么了。”

paragraphs.en: After some time, the ladder was complete. The Tin Woodman assured its strength and readiness. Dorothy, the Scarecrow, Toto, and the Lion climbed up.
paragraphs.zh: 过了一会儿，梯子搭好了。铁皮木人保证了它的稳固和准备情况。多萝西、稻草人、托托和狮子爬了上去。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy had to follow closely behind the awkward Scarecrow.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西只得紧跟在那个笨手笨脚的稻草人身后。

paragraphs.en: When the Scarecrow reached the top, he exclaimed, "Oh, my!" Dorothy followed suit. Then Toto remained silent as they all looked over the wall.
paragraphs.zh: 当稻草人攀上顶端，他惊叫道：“哦，天哪！”多萝西也跟着喊了一声。随后，托托也安静下来，大家望着墙外的景色。

paragraphs.en: The Lion and Tin Woodman also cried out, "Oh, my!" when they saw the strange sight below. They were sitting on a smooth, white floor like the bottom of a platter.
paragraphs.zh: 狮子和铁皮人也惊叫道：“哦，天哪！”当他们看到下面那奇怪的景象时。他们正坐在一块光滑洁白的地面上，就像盘子底部一样。

paragraphs.en: Many small china houses, painted in bright colors, stood around. There were also tiny barns with china fences, and groups of china animals—cows, sheep, horses, pigs, and chickens—all standing nearby.
paragraphs.zh: 许多色彩鲜艳的小瓷房子散落在四周，还有一些小巧的柴房，配着瓷制栅栏。附近还有一群群小瓷动物——牛、羊、马、猪和鸡，都静静地站立着。

paragraphs.en: In the Dainty China Country, travelers encountered peculiar inhabitants: milkmaids in colorful dresses with golden spots, princesses in splendid silver and gold gowns, shepherds in striped knee breeches, princes with jeweled crowns, and clownish figures in ruffled attire. All were tiny, no taller than Dorothy's knee, and made of china.
paragraphs.zh: 在精致瓷国，旅人遇到了一些奇特的居民：穿着彩色衣裙、点缀着金色斑点的奶maid娘、身着华丽银金色礼服的公主、穿着条纹膝裤的牧羊人、戴着宝石王冠的王子以及穿着花边服饰的滑稽人物。他们个头都很小，身高不超过多萝西的膝盖，并且全都由瓷器制成。

paragraphs.en: Initially ignored by the populace, a small purple dog barked at them before retreating. Dorothy asked how to descend from their perch on the wall. The group found the ladder too heavy to lift, so they let Scarecrow fall down first, then jumped onto him to cushion their landings.
paragraphs.zh: 起初，人们并未注意到这只小紫狗，它先是对他们吠叫了一声，然后便退了下去。多萝西询问如何从墙头上下来。众人发现梯子太重，无法抬起，于是让稻草人先摔下去，大家则跳到他身上以缓冲落地的冲击。

paragraphs.en: Once safely down, they restored his shape.
paragraphs.zh: 安全着地后，他们恢复了他的原状。

paragraphs.en: They decided to cross this strange country heading southward. Approaching a china milkmaid milking a china cow, the cow suddenly kicked over its stool and pail, even knocking over the milkmaid herself. The cow broke its leg, the pail shattered into pieces, and the milkmaid had a nick on her elbow.
paragraphs.zh: 他们决定向南穿越这片奇异的土地。当他们走近一位瓷制奶maid正在挤一只瓷牛的场景时，那头瓷牛突然尥蹶子，连同它的尿壶和奶桶一起翻倒在地，奶maid也被撞倒了。瓷牛摔断了一条腿，奶桶碎成了碎片，奶maid的手臂也划破了一道口子。

paragraphs.en: The milkmaid angrily accused them of frightening her cow, causing it to break its leg. Dorothy apologized and asked for forgiveness.
paragraphs.zh: 奶牛女佣气愤地指责他们吓到了她的牛，导致牛瘸了腿。多萝西道歉并请求原谅。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy was deeply concerned about the mishap with the china milkmaid. The kind-hearted Woodman warned, "We must be very careful here; we might hurt these delicate people."
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西非常担心瓷娃娃牛奶女仆的事情。好心的樵夫警告说：“我们必须小心点；我们可能会伤害到这些娇嫩的人。”

paragraphs.en: As Dorothy walked further, she encountered a beautifully dressed Princess who fled at their sight. Curious, Dorothy chased after her, but the Princess cried out, "Don't chase me! Don't chase me!"
paragraphs.zh: 随着多萝西继续前行，她遇到了一位穿着华丽的公主，公主一见到她们便惊慌逃走。多萝西感到好奇，追了上去，但公主喊道：“别追我！别追我！”

paragraphs.en: with a frightened voice.
paragraphs.zh: 带着惊恐的声音。

paragraphs.en: The Princess explained, "If I run, I may fall and break myself." Dorothy asked if she could be mended, to which the Princess replied, "Yes, but I wouldn’t look as pretty after being fixed."
paragraphs.zh: 公主解释说：“如果我跑，可能会摔倒摔碎自己。”多萝西问她是否可以修补好，公主回答道：“可以，但修好了也不会显得那么漂亮了。”

paragraphs.en: Continuing their journey, they met Mr. Joker, one of the clowns, who was always trying to stand on his head. Despite his colorful clothes, he was covered in cracks and had been mended many times.
paragraphs.zh: 继续前行，他们遇到了小丑乔克先生，他总是试图倒立。尽管穿着五彩斑斓的衣服，他的身体上布满了裂痕，显然被修补过多次。

paragraphs.en: The clown said, "My lady fair, why do you stare at poor old Mr. Joker? You're as stiff and prim as if you'd eaten a poker!" The Princess intervened, telling Dorothy not to mind him since he was foolish due to his cracked head.
paragraphs.zh: 小丑说：“我的美人，你为什么盯着可怜的老杰克先生看？你就像吃了一根铁棍一样僵硬和拘谨！”公主插话，告诉多萝西不要介意他的胡言乱语，因为他是因为脑袋摔裂了才变得这么愚蠢。

paragraphs.en: Dorothy assured the Princess she didn’t mind the clown and expressed her admiration for the Princess’s beauty, offering to carry her back to Kansas and place her on Aunt Em's mantel.
paragraphs.zh: 多萝西向公主保证她并不介意那个小丑，并称赞公主的美貌，表示愿意带她回堪萨斯州，把她安置在艾姆姨妈的壁炉台上。

paragraphs.en: The china Princess expressed her unhappiness at the thought of leaving: "That would make me very unhappy." She explained that in their country, they lived freely but stiffened when taken away from their usual places on mantels and cabinets. Dorothy vowed not to cause any distress: "I would not make you unhappy for all the world!"
paragraphs.zh: 瓷国的公主对即将离开表达了不满：“那会使我非常不开心。”她解释说，在她们的国家，人们自由自在地生活，但一旦从壁炉架和柜子上移开就会变得僵硬。多萝西保证不会让她难过：“无论怎样，我都不会让你不开心！”

paragraphs.en: They bid farewell and walked carefully through the china country, where animals and people avoided them out of fear. After an hour, they reached another wall.
paragraphs.zh: 他们道别后，小心翼翼地穿过这个瓷器国，在这里，动物和人们因害怕而避开他们。一小时后，他们来到了另一面墙前。

paragraphs.en: The new wall was lower, allowing them to climb over by standing on the Lion's back. However, in doing so, the Lion accidentally knocked down a china church with his tail, breaking it into pieces. Dorothy lamented: "That was too bad," but added that they were fortunate not to have caused more damage.
paragraphs.zh: 新的围墙较低，他们可以站在狮子背上翻过去。然而，在此过程中，狮子不小心用尾巴碰倒了一座瓷制教堂，将其摔得粉碎。多萝西惋惜地说：“真可惜了，”但她随即补充道，还好没有造成更大的破坏。

paragraphs.en: The Scarecrow noted their good fortune and remarked, "They are indeed brittle." He expressed gratitude for being made of straw, adding, "There are worse things in the world than being a Scarecrow."
paragraphs.zh: 稻草人注意到他们的幸运，说道：“他们确实易碎。”他感激自己是由稻草制成的，并补充道：“这个世界上比稻草人更糟糕的事情还有很多。”
